lean.basis: A leading New Left radical: co-editor of Ramparts from 1968, with close ties to the Black Panthers.

Cast his first Republican vote, for Reagan, in 1984 and went public with "Lefties for Reagan" in 1985; founded the conservative Freedom Center and was a prominent Trump supporter until his death in 2025.

current_role: Founder of the David Horowitz Freedom Center (died April 29, 2025)
summary: David Horowitz (1939–2025) was an American writer and activist who moved from the New Left, where he co-edited Ramparts magazine and worked with the Black Panther Party, to the conservative movement. In 1988 he and Peter Collier founded the Center for the Study of Popular Culture, later renamed the David Horowitz Freedom Center, which published FrontPage Magazine and campaigned on campus politics and against what it called Islamist radicalism; critics, including the Southern Poverty Law Center, accused it of anti-Muslim bigotry. He was a longtime mentor to Stephen Miller. He died on April 29, 2025, at 86.

connections.name: Stephen Miller
connections.description: Horowitz met Miller when Miller, as a Santa Monica High student, campaigned to bring him to speak at the school; Miller later led a Duke chapter of Horowitz's Students for Academic Freedom. Horowitz called Miller his friend and protégé and says he recommended him for jobs with Rep. Michele Bachmann, Rep. John Shadegg and Sen. Jeff Sessions.

sources.title: Stephen Miller, the Firebrand Who Has Survived the White House — PBS FRONTLINE

connections.name: Jeff Sessions
connections.description: Horowitz's Freedom Center gave Sessions its 2014 Annie Taylor Award for Courage; in his speech Sessions credited Horowitz's writing with influencing his thinking. At his 2017 confirmation hearing Sessions called Horowitz "a brilliant writer" but said he was not comfortable with some of his language, and conceded he should have disclosed the award. Horowitz publicly objected to Trump's 2017 attacks on Sessions, and says he recommended Stephen Miller to Sessions.

connections.name: Peter Collier
connections.description: Fellow Ramparts editor and Horowitz's longtime co-author. The two broke with the left together and in 1988 co-founded the Center for the Study of Popular Culture, now the David Horowitz Freedom Center.

connections.name: Ben Horowitz
connections.description: Son. Ben Horowitz, co-founder of the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, is a public figure in his own right; he posted a public tribute when his father died in April 2025.

connections.name: Huey P. Newton
connections.description: In the early 1970s Horowitz became close to Black Panther Party founder Huey Newton and helped the Panthers raise money. He broke with them after the 1974 killing of Betty Van Patter, a bookkeeper he had recommended to the Panthers; the case is unsolved, and Horowitz believed the Panthers were responsible.

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: Horowitz was a prominent Trump supporter: he endorsed Trump and published Big Agenda: President Trump's Plan to Save America (2017). Critics have called him an intellectual godfather of the Trump administration, partly through his protégé Stephen Miller. No source found documents a direct working relationship between the two men.
